Invoke external AI CLIs (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Cursor, Antigravity) to independently review phase plans.
Produces a structured review, shown to the user, with per-reviewer feedback that can be fed back into
**Flow:** Detect CLIs → Build review prompt → Invoke each CLI → Collect responses → Show the review
Cross-AI peer review — invoke external AI CLIs to independently review phase plans.
Each CLI gets the same prompt (PROJECT.md context, phase plans, requirements) and
produces structured feedback. Results are combined into one review, shown and not stored, for the planner
This implements adversarial review: different AI models catch different blind spots.
A plan that survives review from 2-3 independent AI systems is more robust.

Phase number: extracted from the `<arguments>` block (required)
- `--claude` — Include Claude CLI review (uses separate session)
- `--opencode` — Include OpenCode review (uses model from user's OpenCode config)
- `--qwen` — Include Qwen Code review (Alibaba Qwen models)
**No flags** — if `review.default_reviewers` is set, review with only those configured
reviewers that are detected; otherwise review with all available CLIs. Configured
`review.reviewer_instances` names may appear in `review.default_reviewers`; each runs as an
independent reviewer identity backed by its configured adapter+model (see
`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`). Instance names are not valid as flags.
In the shell blocks above, `$PHASE_ID` is `v1.0/02`; `$MILESTONE` is `v1.0` and `$PROJECT` is `taskboard`.

The reviews are shown to the user, not stored: wherever the text above says `REVIEWS.md` is written or committed, read that the combined review is shown in the conversation. `/gsd-plan-phase <phase> --reviews` reads it from there, and its dispositions are recorded as `disposition` rows.

The reviewers are the CLIs of the flags (`claude`, `codex`, `coderabbit`, `opencode`, `qwen`, `cursor`, `agy`, `kimi`) and the local servers (`ollama`, `lm-studio`, `llama-cpp`), run through the shell. Their invocation is the CLI's own: there is no lane manifest, no prompt budget and no lane runner here, so read each CLI's `--help` for the flag that takes a prompt. The settings `review.models.*`, `review.timeouts.*`, `review.effort.*` and `review.max_prompt_tokens*` are declared but inert for that reason: nothing reads them (`review.default_reviewers` is read).

## B. User Prompting
When the workflow needs user input, prompt the user conversationally:
- Present options as a numbered list in your response text
- Ask the user to reply with their choice
- For multi-select, ask for comma-separated numbers
## C. Tool Usage
Use these Cursor tools when executing GSD workflows:
- `Shell` for running commands (terminal operations)
- `StrReplace` for editing existing files
- `Read`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Task`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `TodoWrite` as needed
## D. Subagent Spawning
When the workflow needs to spawn a subagent:
- Use `Task(subagent_type="generalPurpose", ...)`
- The `model` parameter maps to Cursor's model options (e.g., "fast")

## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent that `@gsd/core` does not install** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-security-auditor`, `gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: as the adapter header above says (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
